$comment: The machine-readable index of the kit. Agents read this before reading source. Every package MUST keep its `exports` and `invariants` current; `npm run lint` fails the build if a package exports a symbol that is not listed here.
name: lattice

core.name: @lattice/core
core.purpose: Deterministic primitives. Seeded randomness, noise, maths, easing, typed events, pools, formatting.
invariants: Zero dependencies and zero DOM references.

Two tiers of determinism. Tier A uses only arithmetic ECMA-262 specifies exactly (+ - * /, Math.sqrt, Math.imul, bitwise) and is bit-identical everywhere. Tier B uses sin/cos/pow/exp/log, which the spec does not require to be correctly rounded, and is presentation-only: never hashed, never persisted, never replayed. Every Tier B site declares itself with `@tier-b`.
No module-level mutable state. There is no global Rng, deliberately, and no id counter.
Sub-streams fork from a stream's identity, not its cursor, so a draw made out of order elsewhere cannot reshuffle this one.
Validators return their argument rather than taking a boolean — a boolean has already discarded the value that was wrong, so it cannot name it in the error.

iso.name: @lattice/iso
iso.purpose: Isometric space: the projection, the camera, depth sorting, tile maps, footprints, hit-testing, and grid pathfinding.
invariants: Three coordinate spaces — grid, world, screen — never conflated. Every conversion is a named function.
Tile lookup floors, never rounds.
Hit-testing is computed from state and camera, never cached during a draw pass.

draw.name: @lattice/draw
draw.purpose: The rendering layer: a Surface interface with a Canvas2D backend, colour derivation, and the isometric solid kit that makes procedural art read as designed.
draw.environment: browser (Canvas2D) with an offscreen/headless backend for tests
invariants: Draw calls go through Surface. No package reaches for CanvasRenderingContext2D directly.
A solid is described by one colour; its faces are derived. Shadows cool, highlights warm.
Everything is drawable into an offscreen surface, which is what makes UI thumbnails and golden tests possible.

loop.name: @lattice/loop
loop.purpose: Time. A wall-clock game loop with fixed-step simulation and interpolated rendering, plus scheduling, tweens and frame statistics.
invariants: Simulation advances on the wall clock, never on frame deltas — rAF is 0 Hz in a hidden tab.
Catch-up is clamped; a tab restored after an hour must not run an hour of ticks in one frame.
The clock is injected, so every test runs at whatever speed it likes with no timers.

input.name: @lattice/input
input.purpose: Normalised input: pointer, touch, keyboard and gamepad into one event stream, plus gestures, an action map, and a camera controller.
invariants: Tap and drag are discriminated by distance and time, with the thresholds as named constants.
Zoom is anchored to the pointer.
Every listener returns a disposer. A controller that cannot be torn down leaks a whole game.

audio.name: @lattice/audio
audio.purpose: Sound without assets: WebAudio synthesis from declarative sound definitions, with voice limiting, buses and a music sequencer.
invariants: No AudioContext exists until a user gesture unlocks it.
Silent, not throwing, where there is no WebAudio — importing this in a test is free.
A hard voice ceiling. Summed gains above 1 clip into a click, and twenty voices never sound twenty times better.

persist.name: @lattice/persist
persist.purpose: Saves that survive: versioned state, an explicit migration chain, pluggable storage, debounced writes and integrity checks.
invariants: Every save carries a version and every version has a migration to the next. A save can never be orphaned.
Writes flush on visibilitychange, not on beforeunload — mobile Safari does not reliably deliver the latter.
A corrupt save degrades to a fresh one with a reported reason, never to a thrown exception on boot.

sim.name: @lattice/sim
sim.purpose: Idle-economy mathematics in closed form: cost curves, the flow integrator, offline accrual, and capacity gating.
invariants: Closed form, never a loop. 'Buy max' at 4,000 owned must not be 4,000 iterations on a hot path.
The economy has no tick. State is (stocks, rates, lastTimestamp), integrated on read.
Offline progress warps time, never yield — scaling the output lets a player return with more than their producers could have made.

ui.name: @lattice/ui
ui.purpose: DOM overlay primitives — a declarative element builder, panels, toasts, number rolls, and thumbnails rendered from the draw kit. Deliberately not a framework.
invariants: No virtual DOM. The whole overlay is a few dozen nodes that change a few times a second.
The overlay root is pointer-transparent and re-enables per child, and the child rule out-specifies bare classes.
Anything that is not painting updates on an interval, not inside the frame loop — a hidden tab must not freeze the HUD.
